seal.statement: The production-composed seed host runs CHARGED under the current live calibration lineage (formation-seed-2026-09-17): every owner segment the production attribution seam counts is charged to the node's single core at its calibrated cost, a busy node defers its own events, and the scenario still reaches the simulator's 'Cluster formed' counterpart and then rest. Closure under occupancy is semantic: a phase's consequences get a fixed budget of virtual time measured from when the node is available, never 'so much quiet time'; after teardown the finite queue drains to rest however far occupancy defers it. Charging is off by default and changes WHEN production runs, never WHO owns it: the uncharged path keeps the E/F artifacts and the charged run's provenance snapshot is identical to the uncharged one. Every ambient seam the charged timeline reaches that the uncharged one never did is repaired at its owner through the clock the owner already holds.

text: Q1b CHARGING RESULT. CLOSURE UNDER OCCUPANCY - two host defects found and repaired on the way. (1) A settle horizon recomputed per step from now+50 ms is a moving window: a node whose cadences run continuously never goes quiet, charged or not, and the settle ran 120 virtual s without ending. The budget is now FIXED when the settle begins and measured from max(now, busyUntil): a charged node next event is deferred to its busyUntil, and a budget counted from now would be spent before occupied work ran; uncharged, busyUntil never exceeds now and this is exactly the old rule. (2) The 10000-round non-convergence ceiling is no time at all when charged: the VirtualNetwork re-times each overdue event forward one step at a time (3691 pending after cache hydration took ~3700 rounds at one instant) and then services them a millisecond apart; charged, the ceiling is virtual time (the phase horizon). After teardown nothing regenerates, so the queue is finite and the scenario ends at REST via drainToRest, however far occupancy defers it. host.stop() is now self-driving (drives the scheduler while production tears down inside the node frame, then drains) because the BootstrapService shutdown yield takes the owned clock and is a node timer: bare await host.stop() callers - six composition tests - parked forever on a timer nobody fired until this.

PRODUCTION SEAMS REACHED ONLY ON THE CHARGED TIMELINE. The partition size-update debounce is longer than the 4.451 s uncharged window, so 15.99 s of charged virtual time reached two ambient seams the E/F proofs never could: (a) PartitionService.scheduleSizeUpdate armed its debounced hop with ambient setImmediate (strict violation, owner null, from applyWriteSideEffectPlan under executePartitionRaftWriteCommit); (b) submitPartitionSizeMutation ran runRetryableControlPlaneWrite with the default Date.now deadline and setTimeout sleeps, and stamped updated_at with Date.now. Both are repaired at their owner with the idiom already in the codebase (scheduleRaftPeerReconciliation, service-registration-handoff-owner): a node that owns a clock takes its next turn and its retry deadline from that clock; otherwise setImmediate and Date.now stay. Production defaults unchanged. Red-on-revert: with both seams reverted the charged witness reports violations=1 and the probe measured 1 at seal time (889572cd); restored, 0. Same idiom applied to BootstrapService.shutdown (yieldEventLoopTurn) whose ambient setImmediate the teardown path reached once teardown ran inside the node frame.

ATTRIBUTION LINEAGE UNDER CHARGING (harness and seam).
